name: Action-Constrained RL Robotics Benchmark
description: This study presents a benchmark for evaluating action-constrained reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms. In action-constrained RL, each action taken by the learning system must comply with certain constraints. These constraints are crucial for ensuring the feasibility and safety of actions in real-world systems. We evaluate existing algorithms and their novel variants across multiple robotics control environments, encompassing multiple action constraint types. Our evaluation provides the first in-depth perspective of the field, revealing surprising insights, including the effectiveness of a straightforward baseline approach. The benchmark problems and associated code utilized in our experiments are made available online at github.com/omron-sinicx/action-constrained-RL-benchmark for further research and development.
evaluation_method: Average episodic return (cumulative reward), task success rate, and constraint violation rate (safety metric)
general_score_metric: Average episodic return / task success rate combined with constraint-violation rate (safety-aware performance)
reputation: A recent (2023) specialized benchmark with public code; of growing interest in the constrained-RL and robotics safety community but not yet broadly standardized across RL benchmarks.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark; results can be highly sensitive to simulator, seed, and hyperparameters; different environments use differing constraint definitions so cross-task comparisons require care; moderate community adoption so far.
